pulls.title: fix(weights): release read allocations before completing futures
pulls.body:
## What & why

An asynchronous weight read retains its allocation in the packaged-task closure. Its future can become ready before that closure is destroyed, so `complete()` followed by `close()` can leave the resident-weight budget charged until the worker releases its task. The existing mixed-storage test also intermittently encounters this residual charge.

Move the worker's allocation reference into a local lifetime guard when the task starts. It keeps the buffer alive throughout the read and releases the reference before the task publishes its result, including an error return or exception. Add a regression that completes, checks the loaded bytes and closes 1,000 small weight loads, checking that no completed load retains a resident charge.

## Area

- [x] Engine, CLI or server (`edge0-infer/`)

## How was it tested?

The [isolated before/after validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/Edge0/actions/runs/43949392747/job/133587525602) tests these two files against upstream `f6bfa5546bcf89919f86946ec669bcc7f4cd526d`.

- Before: the first 1,000-load stress run did not reproduce the race; the second left a resident charge after 115 of 1,000 completed loads and failed the regression. The original, unmodified mixed-storage test also reproduced its existing budget assertion failure in [42 of 100 runs](https://github.com/Afloat16/Edge0/actions/runs/43945833532/job/133575120819).
- After: 10 consecutive stress runs, totaling 10,000 completed loads, retained zero charges. Existing shared views, group protection, independent copies and staged admission checks passed.
- Full Linux L0/L1: 98 passed, 3 device skips and the 3 previously reproduced upstream failures (`platform_memory`, `ordered_json`, `template_tools`). All runnable weights tests passed, including lifecycle and staged read-error coverage.
- CPU L2 `weights_compute` and `weights_group_compute`: both passed.
- Local Linux: the regression changed from 14/1,000 residual charges to zero; full L0/L1 had 99 passes, 3 device skips and the 2 existing local environment failures (`app_generation` temporary file and `platform_memory`). Both CPU L2 weights tests passed locally as well.

## Checklist

- [x] Ran affected native and CPU L2 tests.
- [x] Added a regression for the changed behavior.
- [x] Reviewed documentation impact: the patch restores the existing completion and budget-release behavior.

pulls.title: fix(server): retain errors reported inside delegated streams
pulls.body:
## What & why

The delegated engine can report a protocol error after HTTP 200 stream headers have been sent. The proxy forwards that error correctly, but loses its diagnostic fields when recording the request. Chat and Messages then show `stop_reason: unknown`; Responses keeps `failed` but loses the error code. This makes `/status` and recent request history incomplete when diagnosing engine failures.

Retain the error's `code` (falling back to `type`), `message` and `param`, and record the terminal reason as `failed`. The HTTP status and all forwarded bytes remain unchanged. Successful Responses objects with `error: null` retain their normal completion status.

## Area

- [x] Engine, CLI or server (`edge0-infer/`)

## How was it tested?

The [isolated native before/after run](https://github.com/Afloat16/Edge0/actions/runs/43945833532/job/133575120819) tests the exact production changes and regressions in this PR against upstream `f6bfa5546bcf89919f86946ec669bcc7f4cd526d`.

- Before: all three streaming protocols reproduce the missing fields; Chat and Messages also reproduce the unknown stop reason. Three ordinary HTTP-error controls pass.
- After: native regressions pass with complete, seven-byte and one-byte SSE chunks, plus successful `error: null` controls. The HTTP test checks all six requests, recent and last request records, and byte-exact forwarding.
- Full Linux L0/L1: 98 passed, 3 device skips and the 3 reproduced upstream failures (`platform_memory`, `ordered_json`, `template_tools`). Full `ctest --preset cpu --no-tests=error --output-on-failure -L L2 -R strata`: 2 passed.
- A first full run also encountered the existing `weights_mixed` timing failure. The unmodified upstream test reproduced it in 42 of 100 runs in the same validation environment; the final full-suite run did not encounter it. No weights code is changed here.
- Local Linux native and six-request HTTP checks pass. Local full L0/L1 retains the existing temporary-file and platform-memory failures; the production dependency-manifest check passes.

These tests run the real native proxy against the repository's fake engine. They do not require or claim GPU/model execution.

- [x] Ran the affected native and HTTP integration tests.
- [x] Added regression tests for the changed behavior.
- [x] Updated the relevant server documentation.

pulls.title: fix(desktop): preserve selected asset root directories
pulls.body:
## What & why

The directory chooser removes a trailing slash from every selected path. This changes a Windows drive root such as `Z:\` into the drive-relative path `Z:`, and turns the macOS root `/` into an empty string that is treated as cancellation. The selected location is consequently saved and scanned incorrectly, or never added.

Preserve the native chooser's path unchanged. Cancellation still returns no location, and ordinary directories keep their existing behavior.

## Area

- [x] Chat app examples (`edge0-infer/examples/`)

## How was it tested?

[Independent validation on Node 24.15.0 and 26.3.1](https://github.com/Afloat16/Edge0/actions/runs/43938360805): each runtime reproduced **2 failures and 3 passing controls** on upstream, then passed **219 frontend tests** and `npm run build` with this one-line fix.

The regressions mount the actual `App` with ReactDOM, navigate to Models, click Add location, and check the exact path sent to both `save_settings` and `inspect_assets`. They cover a Windows drive root, `/`, ordinary Windows/POSIX directories, and cancellation. The native chooser and persistence boundary are mocked; this does not claim native GUI execution. The component regression harness is retained on the [validation branch](https://github.com/Afloat16/Edge0/blob/b4f9d554989905c2a53b5593035b95e957c14a9c/edge0-infer/examples/desktop/src/asset-location.test.tsx). pulls.title: fix(desktop): clear message edits when conversations change
pulls.body:
## What & why

The desktop chat component keeps its editing index and draft text when the selected conversation changes. If the destination also has a user message at that index, it opens an editor containing the previous conversation's text. pulls.title: fix(model): reject overflowing JSON round-trip candidates
pulls.body:
## What & why

On libstdc++, the shortest-number search can serialize the largest finite binary64 value as `2e+308`. Parsing that candidate saturates to `DBL_MAX` and sets the stream failure flag, but the equality-only check accepts it. A finite JSON value therefore becomes an overflowing representation.

Reject failed round trips that saturated to the maximum finite magnitude and continue searching at higher precision. Keep valid subnormal round trips: libc++ can set the failure flag for subnormal underflow even when the parsed value is correct, so rejecting every failed stream would change existing valid output.

## Area

- [x] Engine, CLI or server (`edge0-infer/`)

## How was it tested?

- [Linux/libstdc++ validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/Edge0/actions/runs/43930624772): reproduced the original `DBL_MAX` failure, then passed **1,030 ordered-JSON comparisons and rejection cases** with this exact fix.
- [macOS/libc++ validation](https://github.com/Afloat16/Edge0/actions/runs/43928604436/job/133514659142): **101 L0/L1 tests passed, 3 Vulkan tests skipped**, and all 1,030 JSON comparisons passed. This includes the smallest signed subnormals as compatibility controls.
- Added positive and negative maximum finite values, their finite neighbors, minimum normal values, signed subnormals, and rejection controls just above the finite range to the existing Python-oracle test, alongside its 1,000 seeded random finite values.
- Local Linux JSON comparisons passed. The full local L0/L1 command also ran in the development checkout, which contains separate cache-accounting and asset-checker changes: **99 passed, 3 skipped**, with the previously reproduced sandbox `std::tmpfile` and Linux platform-memory test failures remaining. An earlier remote Linux full-suite attempt also failed in the unchanged baseline's slots configuration test before reaching the fixed-code step; it is not counted as a successful validation.

## Checklist

- [x] Added numeric-boundary regressions and compatibility controls.
- [x] Ran the affected native JSON probe on Linux and macOS.
- [x] Ran the required L0/L1 command and recorded platform/environment failures separately.

pulls.title: fix(assets): match native manifest parsing in asset checks
pulls.body:
## What & why

`check_assets.py check` can report `passed` for manifests that the native loader rejects or interprets differently. `csv.DictReader` discards surplus fields and blank rows and removes quoting, while Python's integer conversion accepts byte counts containing signs, whitespace, underscores, or non-ASCII digits. Read the catalog as literal tab-separated columns, require exactly four fields and ASCII decimal byte counts, and require an integer format version. Valid leading-zero byte counts remain accepted.

The before/after cases use complete small asset fixtures, not just isolated string predicates. A local probe linked to the actual C++ `open_catalog` confirmed that nine malformed forms rejected by native parsing previously passed the Python checker. For the quoted-role case, native parsing retains the quote characters, whereas the previous checker incorrectly normalized them into the valid `base` role. Normal catalogs and leading-zero counts pass both readers.

Local Python 3.12 also passed all 112 asset unit tests. The full local L0/L1 command was run in the development checkout (which also contains separate JSON and cache-accounting fixes): 99 passed, 3 Vulkan tests skipped, and the two previously reproduced `std::tmpfile` sandbox and Linux platform-memory test failures remained.

pulls.title: fix(desktop): finish streaming at the terminal SSE event
pulls.body:
## What & why

A desktop chat can receive the terminal `data: [DONE]` event while the HTTP response remains open. The client currently waits for transport EOF, keeping the request active until cancellation. It also continues parsing subsequent frames, which can alter the completed answer or raise a JSON error.

Stop consuming the stream at its terminal event and release the reader through the existing cleanup path. Ignore further accumulator input after completion. The regressions cover whole and byte-fragmented responses, retained answer/usage data, reader cancellation, and trailing frames.

## Area

- [x] Chat app examples (`edge0-infer/examples/`)

## How was it tested?

On Linux, Node 24.15.0 and 26.3.1 each reproduced all four new failures against upstream `f6bfa55`, then passed **218 frontend tests** and `npm run build` with this change.

[Before/after validation and full logs](https://github.com/Afloat16/Edge0/actions/runs/43928618071).

The same jobs exercised the real Node HTTP server and native `fetch`: the server sent content, usage, and `[DONE]` without closing the response. Upstream remained active until the 500 ms abort deadline; the fixed client completed in 4.8–6.2 ms with the same answer and metrics. This measures completion of that specific protocol reproduction, not inference performance.

Local Node 24.22.1 also passed all 218 tests, the TypeScript/Vite build, and the native HTTP reproduction.

pulls.title: feat(strata): NVFP4 experts and Q8_0 D/U on Metal for edge0-145b and edge0-120b
pulls.body:
## What & why

On macOS, Edge0 145B and Edge0 120B run only as Q3_K experts with Q4_0 D/U: the Metal runtime has no kernels for the NVFP4 folders or for Q8_0 D/U, and the launcher refuses both before anything starts. This adds them, so a Mac can run the higher-precision build.

Four commits:

1. **`feat(strata)`: the engine.** NVFP4 experts (ggml type 40 for gate, up and down, no column scale, a float32 tail `{s_gate, s_up, s_down, 0}` per expert) and Q8_0 D/U, in the decode windows (`latent_routed.metal`) and in the prompt chain (`DW<T_NVFP4>` for `stage_w` and the whole-layer staging kernel; D/U goes through `dq_f16` of its own type; `mm_gu2`, `mm_down2` and `latent_prompt_gu_f16` scale their sums by the expert's tail). An NVFP4 weight has at most 6 significant bits between 2^-10 and 2880, so its fp16 operand is exact.
2. **`feat(serve)`: the launcher and the docs.** An `fp4` folder starts on Metal, and `du=q8` is accepted. A device's option list can now depend on the expert format (`device_options` key `"<device>/<expert format>"`).
3. **`test(strata)`: `moe_mm_parity` takes `--gu NVFP4 --dn NVFP4`**, with an NVFP4 reference dequantizer in `ref_quant` transcribed from ggml.
4. **`test(strata)`: `latent_routed_parity`**, a parity program for the decode windows' latent kernels, written after `expert_parity`. There was none for either expert format, so it covers Q3_K as well. `dsu_ref_vs_ggml` also checks the NVFP4 reference dequantizer against ggml.

Fixes #245

What macOS does after this:

| Folder | Default D/U | Other choice |
| --- | --- | --- |
| edge0-145b `fp4` | `q8` (the model's own default, as on CUDA) | `du=q4` |
| edge0-120b `fp4` | `q4` (the model's own default, as on CUDA) | `du=q8` |
| `q3k`, both models | `q4`, unchanged | `du=q8`, new |

`ple-io=ram` is still refused on Metal, with the same message. The Q3_K path computes what it did before.

## Area

- [x] Engine, CLI or server (`edge0-infer/`): the launcher, `tools/cli/serve_delegate_registry.cpp`, and its tests
- [ ] Model asset tools (`edge0-infer/tools/assets/`)
- [ ] Chat app examples (`edge0-infer/examples/`)
- [x] Model docs (`docs/`)
- [x] Other: the Metal runtime of `edge0-strata/` (`metal/kernels/`, `metal/src/engine/window.cpp`, `prompt_chain.inc`), its parity programs under `metal/tests/`, the model table of the five READMEs

## How was it tested?

**Machine:** Mac Studio, Apple M5 Max, 128 GB, macOS 27.2, Metal. Built on `main` at `f6bfa55` as `EDGE0.md` describes. The models are the released `Edge0-145B-q3k`, `Edge0-145B-NVFP4` and `Edge0-120B-NVFP4` folders.

**Kernel parity.** All of these print `PASS`; the number is the relative L2 error against the fp16-operand reference:

```
moe_mm_parity --gu Q3_K  --dn IQ4_NL --latent --v2 --stage-gu --tile 32,64,32,2 --T 64                 1.06e-05
moe_mm_parity --gu Q3_K  --dn IQ4_NL --latent --v2 --stage-gu --tile 32,64,32,2 --T 64 --latent1792    1.91e-05
moe_mm_parity --gu NVFP4 --dn NVFP4  --latent --v2 --stage-gu --tile 32,64,32,2 --T 64                 9.76e-06
moe_mm_parity --gu NVFP4 --dn NVFP4  --latent --v2 --stage-gu --tile 32,64,32,2 --T 64 --latent1792    1.34e-05
```

NVFP4 without `--stage-gu`, with tiles 32,64,32,2 and 16,64,64,2 at both widths, gives the same two numbers. Two deliberate kernel errors (the down scale dropped; one nibble given the other sub-block's scale) make it print `FAIL` with 0.28 and 0.67. `ctest` in the Metal build directory: 1 of 1.

pulls.title: perf(strata): map the latent pack files shared on macOS (first prompt of a restart 22 s to 5 s)
pulls.body:
## What & why

On macOS the first prompt after every start of Edge0 145B takes 15 to 23 seconds, whatever its length, where the same prompt later takes under 2. The cause is how the latent pack is mapped.

`src/core/latent_dense.cpp` maps the D/U file and the expert file `PROT_READ, MAP_PRIVATE`, and the Metal engine wraps those mappings as GPU buffers. Measured on a 64 GB M4 Max: after an engine with the private mapping exits, the pack is no longer in the file cache (8 GB of the machine's memory is file-backed), so the next start reads all of it from the SSD again during the first GPU use. With a shared mapping the pack stays cached after exit (47 GB file-backed) and a restart's first prompt takes about 5 s.

One build of `7b60076` with only the flag changed, run in sequence with the unchanged build. Each row is a fresh start; the first 650-token prompt is timed from the engine's log, and `vm_stat` is taken 45 s after the engine stopped:

| Start | Mapping | First prompt | File-backed memory after exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (after a private run) | shared | 19.0 s | 46.7 GB |
| 2 | shared | 5.7 s | 46.6 GB |
| 3 | shared | 5.2 s | 46.6 GB |
| 4 | private | 15.2 s | 8.0 GB |
| 5 | private | 22.8 s | 8.3 GB |
| 6 (after a private run) | shared | 17.6 s | 46.7 GB |
| 7 | shared | 5.3 s | 46.6 GB |

The first start on a cold cache costs the same either way: the pack has to come off the SSD once. While the engine runs the two are alike (50 to 55 GB wired, about 1 GB file-backed), so this does not change the memory the engine needs. Why a read-only private mapping loses the cache I have measured, not traced in the kernel; a pass that binds the buffer makes the whole of it resident, which may be where the private copy is made.

This change maps the two files `MAP_SHARED` on macOS and leaves other platforms on `MAP_PRIVATE`. The mapping is read-only either way and nothing in the tree writes through it. `metal/src/gguf_lite.cpp` already maps the model's main shard `PROT_READ, MAP_SHARED`. The switch is `__APPLE__`, so every macOS user of `LatentDense` and `LatentA` gets it, not only the Metal engine; all of them read through `const` accessors.

Refs #201. 15 lines in `edge0-strata/src/core/latent_dense.cpp`, most of them the comment.

pulls.body:
## What & why

The Windows packages of Edge0 Chat (x64 and Arm64) were built by hand, step by step. This PR adds `scripts/package/windows/package.ps1`, the Windows counterpart of `scripts/package/macos-arm64/package.sh`, so that a Windows package is three commands:

```powershell
.\scripts\package\windows\package.ps1 fetch  -Cache C:\edge0-cache -Commit <commit>
.\scripts\package\windows\package.ps1 build  -Cache C:\edge0-cache -Out C:\edge0-out -Commit <commit>
.\scripts\package\windows\package.ps1 verify -Zip C:\edge0-out\edge0-chat-<version>-windows-<arch>.zip [-Model DIR]
```

- `fetch` downloads the pinned inputs (python.org embeddable Python 3.12.10 with SHA-256, llama.cpp `3cf0325`, the wheels of `edge0-strata/requirements.txt` for the target platform, `cargo vendor`, the npm cache).
- `build` clones the commit clean and builds offline: `edge0-infer.exe` (`windows-vulkan` preset, `GGML_NATIVE=OFF`, static CRT), `strata.exe` / `strata_kq.dll` (as `edge0-strata/EDGE0.md` describes, `STRATA_PORTABLE=ON`, fixed CUDA architectures) and `Edge0 Chat.exe` (`tauri build --no-bundle`, static CRT). It stages the package with the same layout as the 0.2.0 release, writes `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt` and the user README, checks modules, PE machine and build paths, and writes the zip and its `.sha256`.
- `verify` extracts the zip and checks the layout, PE machine, build paths, `edge0-infer info` (`source_modified: no`), `strata.exe --version`, the bundled Python packages and `server.py --help`; with `-Model` it serves one prompt.

The two architectures differ only in a settings table at the top of the script:

| | x64 | Arm64 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| C/C++ compiler | MSVC | clang-cl (with MSVC libraries and linker) |
| GGML CPU code | AVX2, FMA, F16C | `armv8.2-a+dotprod+fp16+i8mm` |
| CUDA architectures | `75;86;89;120` | `121` |
| Wheels / embeddable Python | `win_amd64` / `amd64` | `win_arm64` / `arm64` |

The script runs in the VS developer environment of the machine's CPU; `-EnvScript` loads a script first for toolchains installed outside the usual places. `README.md` in the folder lists the build machine requirements and every step; `user-README.md` is the README inside the package (one template, arch-specific paragraphs kept per arch). The user README also mentions the `Downloads` low-integrity issue we hit on the N1X machine (copy, not move, the zip out of `Downloads`).

It also fixes the Windows build of `main` (one change in edge0-strata): `edge0-strata/src/program/generate.cpp` called `setenv`, which Windows does not have (from 42f3769, #230), so `strata.exe` did not compile on Windows, x64 or Arm64. It now uses `_putenv_s` under `_WIN32`, as the other calls in that file and in `nv_defaults.cpp` / `arch_defaults.cpp` do; Linux and macOS keep `setenv`. A full `-k 0` build of `main` on Windows Arm64 had this as its only failing file (169 of 170 objects compiled).

pulls.title: fix(strata): keep the staged walk off ring slots the open batch still holds
pulls.body:
## What & why

Fixes #206

**Problem.** On a 16 GB card, Edge0-145B-q3k reads prompts between the `--short-read` limit (64 tokens) and 1024 tokens as garbage: an exact-copy prompt comes back reworded, truncated or refused. Longer prompts and prompts of 64 tokens or less are fine, which matches the table in #206.

**Cause.** The fused latent A stage's staged walk (chunks below `stream_all_min()`, `edge0-strata/src/prefill/prefill.cpp`) collects up to `MMQ_GROUP` = 64 experts into one launch. Its staging ring has `stage_n` = `STAGE_GRP` = 32 slots, and the lookahead keeps staging `stage_n - 1` experts ahead of the walk. `stage_one()` reuses slot `n mod stage_n` and makes the copy wait only for the launch that used the slot last. Once the open batch and the lookahead together hold all slots, the next copy overwrites a blob the open batch has not computed with yet, so the batch runs some experts on another expert's weights.

This needs more than `stage_n` non-resident experts between two launches. A card that keeps most experts resident never gets there, which is why the 24 GB report in #206 could not reproduce it.

**Fix.** Count the ring slots that hold a blob no launch has consumed yet (`held`). When all slots are held, the lookahead pauses. When the walk's own expert still has to be staged, the open batch is launched first, which releases its slots. 15 lines, one file. The streamed walk (chunks of 1024 tokens or more) and the non-fused walks are untouched.

A side effect to be aware of: with few resident experts, a batch now closes after at most `stage_n` staged experts instead of `MMQ_GROUP`. Raising `STAGE_GRP` to two groups (as its comment describes) would keep full batches, at the cost of more staging VRAM. I left that decision to you.

## Area

- [ ] Engine, CLI or server (`edge0-infer/`)
- [ ] Model asset tools (`edge0-infer/tools/assets/`)
- [ ] Chat app examples (`edge0-infer/examples/`)
- [ ] Model docs (`docs/`)
- [x] Other: `edge0-strata/` (prompt path)

## How was it tested?

Hardware: RTX A4000 16 GB (sm_86), Windows 11, CUDA 13.5. Model: Edge0-145B-q3k through `edge0-infer serve`. The engine was built from `7b60076` plus this patch. The branch is rebased onto current `main`; the patch applies unchanged, and `main` has not touched the staged walk since.

- **Exact copy** (the request from #206: thinking off, temperature 0, "repeat the text between `<t>` and `</t>` exactly"): exact at every tested prompt length from 67 to 227 tokens. Before the patch, every length above about 70 tokens failed.
- **Long-prompt recall**: 3 of 3 codes returned at prompt lengths up to about 36k tokens, as before the patch.
- **Speed**: about 500 to 780 tok/s prompt reading at 4k tokens, depending on the configuration. No regression measured on long prompts. I did not measure the prompt speed below 1024 tokens before and after.
- **Ruled out before finding the cause**: `STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=0`, `STRATA_SM86_PERF=0` and `--sync-every-layer` did not change the wrong output.
- **Compile check on `main` + patch**: `prefill.cpp` compiles with g++ 13.3 against the CUDA 12.8 headers on Linux (that one file only, not linked or run).

Not tested:

- Linux, and any card other than the RTX A4000 (including the sm_120 card from the report).
- NVFP4 packs and Edge0-120B. I only ran the q3k pack of Edge0-145B.
- A second GPU (`--peer-device`) and the layer split.
- The `ctest` suites. I found no test that covers the staged walk without a GPU and a model, and added none.

## What & why

Fixes #236

The recovery detector never fired on the short "Hmm" turns: `reasoning_repeat_coverage` returned 0.0 until the reasoning held 2,000 words, so the 71 turns of 512-2,559 tokens in the report were all missed. The window is now the whole reasoning once it holds 300 words (new `LOOP_MIN_WORDS`), so a few hundred words of one repeated filler is caught at the first check. Below 300 words it still returns 0.0, since one repeated passage weighs too much against the 0.25 bar there to call it a loop. Long-turn behavior is unchanged.

## Area

- [x] Other (edge0-strata/serve)

pulls.title: strata(split): the draft layer's token embedding on a layer split
pulls.body:
A layer split puts the draft layer on the last stage, and its prompt pass gathers the token embedding there.  Two things made that an illegal memory access:

1. The native embedding table is one singleton, placed in the current card's VRAM by STRATA_EMBED_VRAM=1 (the first card).  The drafter's gather kernel on another card read that VRAM: an IMA on the first request, and one that only shows up with --mtp (without it nothing on the later card touches the table).  A split now keeps the table in mapped host memory, which every card can read; the log says why when STRATA_EMBED_VRAM=1 is set.

2. The fallback path was broken too: a later stage's weight table carries no token_embd (it is the first layer's tensor, not resident there), so reading it gathered from a null pointer.  The check now covers the data pointer and only on the path that reads the weights.

Diagnostics kept behind env switches, they are how this was found: STRATA_MTP_DEV=1 (which card each of the drafter's buffers is on), STRATA_MTP_CALL_SYNC=1 (is a device already dirty before the drafter runs: the CUDA failure is sticky, so a fault elsewhere used to read as the drafter's) and STRATA_MTP_STEP_SYNC=1 (which step of the prompt pass).

Measured on 2 x RTX 5090 D over PCIe (canAccessPeer = 0), --layer-split 24 --prefill 256, Q4 D/U pair: Edge0 145B NVFP4 and Q3_K both answer 17*23 = 391 with --mtp on (about 82 tok/s decode), where before they aborted at the first request.  Single GPU on the same build, both packs: 391.  Paths without MTP (--split-device 0, --peer-device 1, single GPU) are unchanged and were re-measured.

pulls.title: perf(strata): lend the Metal prompt chain's chunk buffers to the OS between prompts on latent packs
pulls.body:
## What & why

The Metal prompt chain reserves its chunk buffers once and keeps them until teardown. Beside Edge0 145B at 1024 rows that is about 4.5 GB that sits idle between prompts on a machine where the pack already takes most of the memory: on a 64 GB Mac it ends up in swap.

The buffers are scratch: a chunk writes what it reads, except two grid constants in `meta` that `pc_setup` writes once. So between prompts this change makes them volatile (`setPurgeableState`, through a small `Context::set_idle`): macOS may discard them under memory pressure instead of swapping them out, and they are taken back, with the two constants written again, before the next prompt. Without memory pressure nothing is discarded. `STRATA_METAL_PROMPT_KEEP=1` keeps them as they are, and `docs/MAC.md` lists it. Only latent packs are affected.

`set_idle` acts only on a whole buffer from `alloc()`: it leaves a chunked wrap and a view onto another allocation alone. `Window::prompt` returns after its command buffers have completed, so no GPU work references the buffers when they become volatile. A prompt after a discard pays for faulting the pages back in as zeros; that cost is not measured here, because nothing in these runs reports whether a discard happened.

Refs #201.

pulls.title: fix(strata): give back the host code's unused device weight copies on Metal latent packs
pulls.body:
## What & why

On a latent pack the Metal window reads the model from the wrapped files and keeps its own KV. The device allocations the shared host code makes before that (among them the dense weight copies, the session's KV pool and the expert cache slots: 53 allocations, 4.98 GB at 32K) are not read by the window. They stay allocated: 4.7 GB at the template's 32K context, 7.3 GB at 131,072 and 10.8 GB at 262,144, because the KV pool grows with the context. Beside a pack that fills a 64 GB Mac that memory can only live in the compressor and the swap.

This change gives them back at the end of latent setup with `purge_device_allocations`, the call `stream_arena` makes for SSD streaming. `STRATA_METAL_KEEP_HOST_WEIGHTS=1` keeps them, as it does there.

Where it differs from the streaming path, so it can be judged:

- **Threshold.** It gives back host device allocations of 16 MiB and more; `stream_arena` uses 32 MiB. The band between holds 48 allocations of 27.9 and 33.4 MB (1.41 GB together) that the streaming path keeps; the five above 32 MiB are 3.58 GB. I found no reader of them on the latent path and the outputs below are unchanged, but the streaming precedent does not cover them. Raising it to 32 MiB keeps most of the saving if you prefer the proven line.
- **Timing.** It runs inside `Window::init`, earlier than `stream_arena`, which runs at the first prompt or decode. Everything the host allocated up to that point is affected; allocations made later are not.
- **The guard.** `check_purged` stops a host copy or fill that touches a given-back allocation. A read through `host_view`, `buffer_for_cpu_impl` or a raw kernel argument is not guarded and would see zeros. In the `strata` binary the only `host_view` caller I found is the M-RoPE table, which is far below the threshold at any supported context.
- **Accounting.** If Metal still counts emptied buffers in `currentAllocatedSize`, the free-memory figure the host derives from it does not rise by the amount given back. That errs towards refusing work, and on this machine the figure reads 0 MiB with or without the change.

pulls.title: fix(strata): count tool-call-only answers in the community bench
pulls.body:
## What & why

Fixes #222

`tools/strata_bench.py` reports `FAILED: no token came back` for agent-session turns that the model answers with **only a tool call**. The agent test offers four tools. With thinking off, such an answer streams nothing but `delta.tool_calls`:

```
finish_reason: tool_calls   completion_tokens: 26   delta fields with data: {'role': 1, 'tool_calls': 8}
```

`chat()` only counts `delta.content` and `delta.reasoning_content` as a token, so `first` stays `None`, `digest()` marks the turn not ok, and the session stops there. The engine did answer: the failed turns had 26–49 generated tokens.

I hit this with `edge0-145b` on an RTX 3090 at a 16 GiB VRAM budget. 2 of 3 agent sessions failed this way in one run and 3 of 3 in another. At 24 GiB the model happened to answer in text. The same line is in upstream Strata, and the symptom appears in an RX 9070 XT report there (Niko1221/Strata#2876, closed in the tracker reset).

The fix follows the semantics agreed in #222:

- the first-token time is set by the first non-empty delta of any kind (`content`, `reasoning_content`, `tool_calls`);
- `pieces` keeps counting text only, so `generated_tokens` still falls back to the engine's `usage` and never to the number of tool-call chunks.

The turn's text stays content only, and the session already falls back to `"Understood."` for an empty reply.

## Area

- [ ] Engine, CLI or server (`edge0-infer/`)
- [ ] Model asset tools (`edge0-infer/tools/assets/`)

- [x] Other — `edge0-strata/tools/strata_bench.py` (the community bench)

## How was it tested?

- New test `SuiteTests.test_a_tool_call_answer_counts_as_an_answer`: `FakeStrata` gets a mode that answers requests offering tools with `tool_calls` deltas only. It fails before the change with `[{'where': 'agent', 'error': 'no token came back'}]` and passes after.
- New test `SuiteTests.test_tool_call_chunks_are_not_counted_as_text`: `chat()` on a tool-call-only answer sets `first`, and `pieces` stays 0 (it would be 12 if tool-call chunks were counted).
- `python -m unittest test_strata_bench` in `edge0-strata/tools/`: 24 tests OK.
- Against the real engine (edge0-strata 0.1.55, Edge0-145B-q3k, Linux, RTX 3090), measured with the first commit: a tool-call only answer now counts as an answer: ok, first token after 613 ms, 26 generated tokens (from the engine's usage), empty text. pulls.title: fix(strata): keep every lane in the latent D kernel's warp reductions (prefill hang on DGX Spark)
pulls.body:
## What & why

**Motivation.** On a DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121), Edge0-145B NVFP4 prompts hang in prefill: the serve watchdog fires with `no progress for 60 s during a request (reading the prompt (batched): layer 0 of the prompt chunk from token 0)` and restarts the engine. It happens on most prompts but not all, so it looks random. The only workaround is `STRATA_LATENT_FUSED_DU=0`, which drops prefill from ~900 to ~210 tok/s.

**Cause.** In `latent_dense_kernel<true>` (the latent D projection, in `moe_fused.cu` and its copy in `moe_fused_q3k.cu`), the epilogue does

```cpp
const int r_t = nb0 + 8 * n + 2 * tig + qc;   // the token's tile row
if (r_t >= nrows) continue;
...
am = fmaxf(am, __shfl_xor_sync(0xffffffffu, am, 16));   // full-warp shuffles
```

When the last 64-row tile is only partly filled, lanes whose row is past the end skip the full-mask `__shfl_xor_sync` calls that the other lanes of the warp wait in. That is undefined behaviour; on sm_121 the warp deadlocks. Whether a prompt hits it depends on its token count mod 64, hence the intermittency.

**Change.** Every lane runs the reductions; only lanes with a real row store (`const bool valid = r_t < nrows;` and `if (!valid) continue;` after the shuffles, before the stores). The shuffles (xor 4, 8, 16) only combine lanes with the same `tig`, so the same token row: a row past the end only ever feeds itself, and the tile's spare rows repeat its last row (`srow`), so their values are finite. Rows of full tiles are unchanged bit for bit (checked below). Two commits:

1. `fix(strata)`: the fix in both kernels (4 lines each).
2. `test(strata)`: `lat_dense_d_tail_test`, a regression test registered with CTest.

No existing issue; I can open one if you prefer to track it there.

## Area

- [ ] Engine, CLI or server (`edge0-infer/`)
- [ ] Model asset tools (`edge0-infer/tools/assets/`)
- [ ] Chat app examples (`edge0-infer/examples/`)
- [ ] Model docs (`docs/`)
- [x] Other: `edge0-strata/` (prefill kernels)

## How was it tested?

Environment: NVIDIA DGX Spark (GB10, sm_121, 128 GB unified memory), DGX OS 7.2.3 / Ubuntu 24.04, kernel 6.17 (nvidia), driver 595.91.07, CUDA 13.0 toolkit. Base commit `b7900cb`. Engine built per `edge0-strata/EDGE0.md` with `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=121`.

| Check | Before (b7900cb) | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lat_dense_d_tail_test` (both kernels, Q8_0 / Q4_0 / q3k colscale, M = 1..127) | hangs at the first partial tile (M=1), 3 of 3 runs | PASS |
| `compute-sanitizer --tool memcheck` on the test | n/a (hangs) | 0 errors |
| `compute-sanitizer --tool synccheck` on the test | hangs first, reports nothing | 0 errors |
| Full tiles (M=128), old vs new kernel output, all 4 variants | | byte-identical (8.3 MB, same SHA-256) |
| Edge0-145B NVFP4, 10 prompts of 4K-32K tokens, fused D/U on | most hang (watchdog restart) | 10 of 10, prefill 850-1030 tok/s |
| Edge0-145B NVFP4, agent client with ~38K-token prompts, multi-turn | hangs, or ~210 tok/s with `STRATA_LATENT_FUSED_DU=0` | completes; 38K tokens read in 41 s (940 tok/s) |

Not covered: I only have sm_121, so this was not run on RTX cards. There it is the same undefined behaviour that happens to complete; full-tile output is unchanged and the partial-tile rows are the same rows, so no change in results is expected. The q3k kernel is covered by the unit test only (no Q3_K model run end to end).

<details>
<summary>cuda-gdb on the hung test, unpatched (built with -lineinfo)</summary>

```
[Switching focus to CUDA kernel 0, grid 5, block (0,0,0), thread (0,0,0), device 0, sm 0, warp 2, lane 0]
0x0000000325b0aa40 in strata::prefill::fused::(anonymous namespace)::latent_dense_kernel<true><<<(48,1,1),(512,1,1)>>> ()
  at .../sm_30_intrinsics.hpp:449 in __shfl_xor_sync inlined from moe_fused.cu:1170
  Kernel Parent Dev Grid Status       SMs Mask  GridDim  BlockDim Invocation
*      0      -   0    5 Active 0x000003030303 (48,1,1) (512,1,1) strata::prefill::fused::(anonymous namespace)::latent_dense_kernel<true>()

Device 0 SM 0
```

# What & why

`edge0-145b` is documented as NVIDIA-only. `edge0-strata` still carries upstream Strata's HIP backend, but the
latent-MoE additions did not build or run with it. With the changes below Edge0-145B-q3k loads, reads prompts and
decodes on a Radeon RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100, 24 GB) under Windows 11.


Build (HIP only):

- `CMakeLists.txt`: the HIP MMQ branch now compiles `lat_q3k_*.cu` and `moe_fused_q3k.cu` (their entry points are
  already stubs under `__HIPCC__`), and `strata_engine` gets `latent_dense.cpp` and `latent_moe.cpp` on HIP too; they
  were only added inside `if(STRATA_ENABLE_CUDA)`.
- `moe_fused.cu`, `moe_fused_q3k.cu`: the `latent_kernel` / `latent_kernel_q3k` launches were outside the
  `!__HIPCC__` guard that holds the kernels. They are not reached on HIP (`lat_dev().ok` is false).
- `verify.cpp`, `prefill.cpp`: two debug dumps use `cudaGraph*` / `cudaPointer*` names the HIP shim does not map.

Run (HIP only):

- `verify.cpp`: the D stage's two D2H `cudaMemcpyAsync` calls and the "verify top3" dump (a synchronous
  `cudaMemcpy`) ran inside the verify window's graph capture. HIP then fails every request with
  `verify: end capture: operation failed due to a previous error during capture`. On HIP the two copies go through
  `copy_bytes_from_mapped` and the dump is skipped.

Every code change is inside `#if defined(STRATA_USE_HIP)` / `__HIPCC__` or in the HIP branch of the CMake file, so
the CUDA build's sources are unchanged after preprocessing.

Docs: `EDGE0.md` gets a "Build (Windows, AMD, experimental)" section.

Limits:

- The fused latent kernels stay CUDA-only. On HIP the model runs with `STRATA_LATENT_FUSED=0`,
  `STRATA_LATENT_FUSED_DU=0`, `STRATA_LAT_FUSED_Q3K=0`, so the prompt speed is far below the NVIDIA figures.
- `edge0-infer` does not start this build; the server is started by hand with a configuration file.
- `labels.bin` is located by the last `/` of `STRATA_LATENT_A`, so a path with only `\` fails. Not changed here;
  the documentation says to write the path with `/`.

Environment: Windows 11 (10.0.26300), Ryzen 7 5800X3D, 64 GB RAM, Radeon RX 7900 XTX 24 GB, driver
32.0.31041.1004, ROCm 10.2.0a20260930 (TheRock wheels), Visual Studio Build Tools, base commit b7900cb.

Passed:

- HIP build: `set STRATA_HIP_ARCHS=gfx1100`, `set STRATA_NO_VISION=1`, `tools\hip\build_windows.bat` (targets

pulls.body:
<!-- Thanks for contributing to edge0! Keep this short but complete. -->

## What & why

Fixes found while accepting the 0.2.0 Windows arm64 release on an RTX Spark (N1X) machine.

**Desktop app: keep enough commit memory for generation** (`b1fac34`)

On a GPU that shares system memory, Windows charges VRAM allocations to the commit limit (RAM + page file). edge0-strata's `--expert-cache auto` fills the free VRAM, so the official Edge0 145B Q3K left ~0.5 GB of commit free after loading on a 128 GB machine (66.5 GB visible to Windows, 102.5 GB commit limit). The first request commits ~6.5 GB more, and the engine crashed with an out-of-memory error. It worked only after retries, when a dying engine still held VRAM at start-up and the new cache came out ~9 GB smaller.

Without changing the engine or the machine, the app now:

- waits after the ready line until the committed memory has been steady for 3 s (at most 30 s) before reporting the model loaded;
- when less than 10 GiB is left, reloads the engine with `--strata-arg --vram-reserve-mib N` sized to the shortfall (at most twice, up to 24 GiB), and remembers N per model in `memory-reserve.json` so later loads start with it;
- stops reloading a model when a reload frees no commit memory (a GPU with its own memory);
- shows an English warning when less than 8 GiB is still free, and adds the likely cause to the error when the engine dies mid-generation.

Only models run by edge0-strata get the reserve; macOS has no commit limit and skips the check. A smaller cache drops the least used experts: an engine that started with ~9 GB less cache decoded at 34.4 tok/s against 34.1–34.7 tok/s with a full one.

**Desktop app** (`cfe48bd`, `11d9abd`): use the `edge0-infer` beside the app when no executable is set; read the engine status once a model is loaded so the sidebar names the device.

**Docs** (`2b735d6`, `57d6840`): link the Edge0 145B and 120B Hugging Face repositories; drop the stale `start.sh` / `model-bench.json` note.

pulls.title: fix(serve): treat null optional request fields as absent
pulls.body:
## What & why

The OpenAI API marks most optional request fields as nullable (`temperature`, `top_p`, `max_tokens`, `stop`, `seed`, `n`, `stream_options`, `reasoning_effort`, `instructions`, `max_output_tokens`, `reasoning`, ...), and clients use `null` to mean "not set". `portal::parse` only accepts `null` for `metadata`. For every other field it checks the type, so a request that sends

```json
{"model": "test", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}], "temperature": null, "stop": null}
```

is rejected with `400 Expected a number: temperature`. The same request with the field left out works.

This PR drops `null` values of those fields before validation, so `null` behaves exactly like leaving the field out:

- The list follows each protocol's own allowed fields: shared fields, plus Chat-only fields (`seed`, `stop`, `max_tokens`, `max_completion_tokens`, `n`, `logit_bias`, `logprobs`, `stream_options`, `presence_penalty`, `frequency_penalty`, `reasoning_effort`) or Responses-only fields (`instructions`, `max_output_tokens`, `include`, `reasoning`, `truncation`, `background`).
- A `null` unknown field, a `null` field that belongs to the other protocol (`max_output_tokens` on Chat, `seed` on Responses), and a `null` required field (`model`, `messages`, `input`) are still rejected as before.
- Extensions (`top_k`, `repetition_penalty`, `chat_template_kwargs`, `promptCacheKey`) and fields OpenAI doesn't mark nullable (`tools`, `tool_choice`, `response_format`, `text`) keep their current strict checks.
- The Responses echo uses the cleaned request, so `"reasoning": null` echoes the default `{"effort": null, "summary": null}` object, the same as an omitted `reasoning`.

`docs/openai-compatible-server.md` gets one sentence about this under "Request compatibility".

pulls.title: fix(server): keep string-typed tool-call arguments as strings
pulls.body:
## Problem

Both checkpoint chat templates write a tool-call argument bare when it is a string and as `tojson` otherwise (`v if v is string else v|tojson` in Ling, `args_value | string if args_value is string else args_value | tojson` in Qwen3.5). `_coerce` reverses that by trying `json.loads` on every value, but a string parameter whose text is also valid JSON can't be told apart that way. For a tool declared with `"zip": {"type": "string"}` and `"flag": {"type": "string"}`:

```
<tool_call>
<function=lookup>
<parameter=zip>
10001
</parameter>
<parameter=flag>
true
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
```

On `main` this comes back as `function.arguments == '{"zip": 10001, "flag": true}'`. The client gets a number and a bool for parameters its own schema says are strings: ids, zip codes, phone numbers, version strings like `2`, or the word `true` / `null`. A client that validates arguments against the schema rejects the call.

## Fix

- The request's `tools` are now passed to the parser: `app._extract_tool_calls` calls `engine.parse_tool_calls(content, tools=req.tools)`, and both engines forward it to `parse_ling_tool_calls` / `parse_qwen_tool_calls`. The new parameter is optional and defaults to `None`.
- `_parse_arguments` returns the raw strings. `_split` then looks up the called function in `tools`, keeps parameters declared `"type": "string"` exactly as written, and runs `_coerce` on everything else as before.
- If the function isn't in `tools`, has no `parameters.properties`, or `tools` is missing or malformed, every value goes through `_coerce` as it does today.

## Tests

pulls.title: fix(server): keep NaN and Infinity tool-call arguments as strings
pulls.body:
## What & why

`server/tool_calls.py` turns each bare argument value into JSON with `json.loads` (so `5` becomes a number and `{"a": 1}` an object) and otherwise keeps it as a string. But Python's `json.loads` also accepts `NaN`, `Infinity` and `-Infinity`. So a tool call whose argument text is one of those words, for example a search for `NaN`, gets a float, and `_to_openai` then writes `function.arguments` with `json.dumps`, which emits the bare tokens:

```
<tool_call>search<arg_key>query</arg_key><arg_value>NaN</arg_value></tool_call>
-> "arguments": "{\"query\": NaN}"
```

That string is not valid JSON, so an OpenAI client (`JSON.parse`, or `json.loads` with strict constant handling) fails to read the tool call. It affects both the Ling (edge0-8b) and Qwen3.5 (edge0-35b) dialects. The chat templates render non-string values with `tojson`, which never writes these words, so treating them as plain strings matches the template.

This PR passes `parse_constant` to `json.loads` in `_coerce` so those three words stay strings (`{"query": "NaN"}`). Numbers, booleans, `null`, objects and arrays are coerced as before.

No issue filed; I found this while reading `server/tool_calls.py`.

pulls.title: fix(server): answer a malformed or non-object request body with 400
pulls.body:
## What & why

A request body that is not valid JSON, or is valid JSON but not a chat request, gets no usable answer:

- **stdlib transport:** `do_POST` runs `json.loads` outside any `try`, so a malformed body (`{not json`, or bytes that are not UTF-8) raises inside the handler. The client sees the connection closed with no HTTP response, while the Flask transport and the other validation errors answer 400 `invalid_request`.
- **Both transports:** `parse_chat_request` assumes the shape. `[1, 2]`, `"hello"`, `{"messages": "hi"}`, `{"messages": ["hi"]}` and `{"messages": [null]}` raise `AttributeError` from `.get`, which is a 500 on Flask and a dropped connection on stdlib.

This PR makes the stdlib handler answer a malformed body with 400 (`request body is not valid JSON: ...`), and makes `parse_chat_request` raise the same `ValueError` the other bad inputs raise (`request body must be a JSON object`, `messages must be a list of message objects`), so both transports answer 400 before any generation or SSE headers.

pulls.title: fix(server): flush a trailing U+FFFD at the end of a chat stream
pulls.body:
## Problem

`_chat_stream` documents that the concatenated deltas equal the non-streaming text. The incremental decode holds back a trailing U+FFFD on the assumption that a later id will complete the character, which is correct mid-stream. The final flush goes through `_incremental_suffix` too, though, and that also strips the trailing U+FFFD. When a generation ends on an incomplete character (for example a byte-level BPE model hitting `max_tokens` partway through a multi-byte character), the non-streaming response ends in `\ufffd` but the stream drops it, so the two disagree.

## Fix

Once generation has finished, no later id can complete the character. The tail flush now emits `final[len(emitted):]` directly when the emitted text is a prefix, and keeps the existing `_incremental_suffix` path otherwise.

## Test

`test_chat_stream_flushes_trailing_replacement_char_at_end` uses a tokenizer whose last id decodes to U+FFFD. Before the fix, the stream yields `"ok fine"` while non-streaming yields `"ok fine\ufffd"`, and the test fails. With the fix, it passes.

I don't have Apple Silicon/MLX, so I ran `tests/test_server.py` with the `mlx`/`mlx_lm` imports stubbed: 50 passed, 3 skipped. The new test fails without the fix. CI on macOS should confirm.

pulls.body:
## What & why

Adds an on-device benchmark for Android. BenchTest is an instrumented test that measures decode
speed, prefill speed and peak memory of a model on a real phone and prints the submission block
used by the Hardware Benchmarks discussion (runtime: android). tools/bench/run_bench.sh runs it
through adb and prints only the block, so one command gives a paste-ready result. README section
1.7 documents the runner, the protocol, every block field and troubleshooting.

    bash tools/bench/run_bench.sh --8b --reporter @your-handle

Fixes #141

## Area

- [x] Android (`android/`)

## Protocol

- One cold warmup run, then 2 measured runs over a fixed ~3.3k-token prompt (the BENCH_LONG
  paragraphs of python/examples/bench.py), thinking off. The block reports the mean of the 2
  measured runs; the notes list the cold run and each run, with its own peak memory.
- Every run must decode exactly 200 tokens. This is deliberate: it measures an extended decode,
  and the engine reports a failed decode as a normal, shorter answer (see below), so an early stop
  fails the run instead of reporting a shorter window. The engine cannot be told to ignore
  end-of-sequence, so a model that ends its answer early also fails the run.
- Sampling: temperature 0.2 by default (the app's own default); --temperature 0 is greedy.
- Peak memory is the process's resident peak (VmHWM), reset before each run through
  /proc/self/clear_refs; if the phone refuses, it falls back to the whole-process maximum.
- Device model, SoC, RAM and Android version are collected automatically. engine_commit comes
  from vendor.llama.pin.
- The test also runs as a Gradle connected test (documented in README 1.7). Gradle uninstalls the
  APKs at the end, which removes the staged model.

## Differences from python/examples/bench.py

The cold run is kept apart from the mean instead of reporting two runs; there is no 10-token
untimed decode warmup (it needs an engine change); a run that stops before 200 tokens fails;
only the temperature is applied when sampling (see below); peak memory is the resident peak, not
MLX's allocator peak. Table in README 1.7.

## How was it tested?

- 74 JVM unit tests (protocol, block, device helpers) pass; the instrumented test compiles.
- Runner script checked against a fake adb (success, failure, quoting, no device).
- Galaxy S23 (8 GB, Android 16), 8B tier, through the Gradle route, output verbatim:

      tier:            edge0-8b
      runtime:         android
      device:          Samsung SM-S911U
      soc:             Snapdragon 8 Gen 2
      ram_gb:          8
      os:              Android 16 (API 36)
      decode_tok_s:    1.14
      prefill_tok_s:   10.3
      peak_active_gib: 3.40
      engine_commit:   7ab4ee7baad2d920464cbacfad4f4b07cf111fd2
      reporter:        @your-handle
      notes:           cold run: decode 1.80 tok/s, prefill 10.4 tok/s, peak 3.54 GiB; run 1: decode 1.56 tok/s, prefill 10.0 tok/s, peak 3.33 GiB; run 2: decode 0.72 tok/s, prefill 10.7 tok/s, peak 3.40 GiB; 3301-token prompt, 200 decoded, mean of 2 reps, temperature 0.2

  The 5 GB model does not fit in this phone's free memory, so throughput is memory-bound.
- Not tested: the 35B tier (needs a 12 GB+ phone).

## Found while building this (not fixed here)

1. llama_chat.c reports a failed decode as success: after each token a failing llama_decode

pulls.title: fix(android): make the android tree usable from non-Windows clones
pulls.body:
## Problem

Two host-portability breaks make `android/` unbuildable from any Linux/macOS clone, and
  both bite before a single line of project code runs:

  1. `android/gradlew` is committed as mode **100644** while `android/gradlew.bat` is 100755.
     README 1.3 tells the reader to run `./gradlew :app:assembleDebug`; on Linux/macOS that is
     `permission denied`, exit code **126**, with Gradle never starting.
  2. `android/tools/llama/build_vendor_libs.sh` resolves the monorepo root with `pwd -W`, a
     Git-Bash (MSYS) only form. On other POSIX shells the builtin rejects `-W`, the command
     substitution returns non-zero, and `set -euo pipefail` aborts at the depot line -
     **silently, with no log output**, so it reads as "the script is broken" rather than
     "wrong host".

  ## Changes

  - Set the exec bit on `android/gradlew` **in the index**, not just on disk: a local `chmod`
    leaves the next clone exactly as broken as this one. The repo already tracks modes
    (`ios/scripts/test.sh`, `macos/scripts/*.sh`, `python/scripts/fetch_models.py` are all
    100755), so this is a missing bit rather than a policy change.
  - `DEPOT=${EDGE0_DEPOT:-$(cd "$REPO/.." && { pwd -W 2>/dev/null || pwd -P; })}` - Git-Bash
    semantics untouched (the `-W` form wins wherever it exists), other hosts get the resolved
    path, and `EDGE0_DEPOT` still overrides but is no longer required to be exported.
  - `docs(android)`: host unit-test count `26 -> 32` in all five language copies.

| path | text |

| base, streaming | 9 U+FFFD, no emoji |
| head, streaming | 🌊🏖️🦀🍣 (0 U+FFFD) |

…-35b

A memory-starved host (16 GiB RAM, 19.7 GB 35b checkpoint) spends each decode step in ~3000 MAJOR faults, i.e. the step degrades into "cold pages x per-fault latency" (217 ms / 3079 = 70 us), while the bandwidth floor is only 26 ms (49 MiB @ 1.88 GB/s). Those demand faults serialize on the VM map lock, so moving expert loads to a background pool does not by itself buy anything.

Changes:
- mmap.SafetensorsMmap.advise_willneed_range(offset, length): page-aligned MADV_WILLNEED over ONE byte range. The existing advise_willneed() only covered a whole shard.
- layer.StreamingMoELayer.warm_experts_willneed(experts): one hint per (expert, tensor) byte range, issued before the build in prefetch() and stage_experts(). Retains no MLX arrays, so it does not displace the page cache. (warm_pages() is pre-existing dead code and demand-faults synchronously via sl.sum(); left untouched.)
- LayerOptions.warm_willneed, default False.
- staged_k4(): enable the existing incr_stack + incr_writeback switches together with warm_willneed. incr_stack replaces the per-step core.stack with persistent in-place tensors and incr_writeback keeps the staged bundles out of the shared LRU, removing duplicate copies of the staged set.

Measured on edge0-35b (16 GiB M2, 60-step sampled REPLAY with 20 untimed warmup steps, cache_slots=64, 5 rounds, rotated arm order, paired per round; replay feeds both arms the SAME token sequence so the work is identical):

                        step        tok/s

  shipped default       244.25 ms   4.09
  prerouter=None        264.06 ms   3.79

  new vs shipped      : -56.8 ms median, 4/5 paired  -> +31.0%
  prerouter gain      : +8.0% -> +37.8% (5/5 paired)

- All numbers come from one 16 GiB M2. incr_writeback keeps staged bundles out of the shared LRU, which is free here (LRU hits ~0 at 64 slots) but needs revalidation on a larger-memory host where the LRU actually hits.

pulls.body:
## What

`--no-prerouter` did not actually take the exact path, and the 8b tier never harvested.

**1. Switch semantics (`--no-prerouter`)**
With `prerouter=None`, `options.staged` stayed `True`, so every layer kept staged slots -- filled from history (the previous token's actual top-k). That silently zeroes every routed expert outside the slot set: `staged_dropped = 3593` for a single edge0-8b request, ~2/3 of the experts per step on edge0-35b (this is also where the earlier "`--no-prerouter` is 34% faster" reading came from). Now staged slots are only kept by layers whose ROUTE is a prerouter prediction (the consumers, `start_layer+1 ..`); with `prerouter is None` no layer keeps slots, so the off path is the exact path. `history_slots=True` / `--history-slots` stays the opt-in legacy behaviour.

**2. edge0-8b parity with the 35b tier** -- per-request reset of `m_in_cache` / `last_topk` / `prev_topk_oh` (+ `pg_cache`), the first decode step's prediction is no longer overwritten by the last prefill actuals, and non-consumer layers leave the staged path. `prod_k8()` now defaults to `staged=True` (`cache_slots` stays 64 for the low-memory profile).

**3. Demo defaults** -- `edge0 demo` / `examples/demo.py` run edge0-8b on the gate-routed exact path (`Ling8BConfig.demo_no_prerouter` + `registry.demo_kwargs`); `chat` / `serve` keep the tier default. One switch only: `--no-prerouter`.

pulls.title: Add opt-in persistent conversation checkpoints
pulls.body:
Repeated coding conversations currently recompute their full prompt after each request or process restart. This adds opt-in persistent inference checkpoints so the server and Python engine can restore the longest saved token prefix and process only the unmatched suffix.

The implementation uses a radix index backed by SQLite, immutable shared safetensors KV blocks, and checkpoint-specific recurrent, logits, and prerouter state. It includes namespace fingerprints, checksums, atomic publication, cross-process locking, bounded LRU eviction, exact-message tokenization caching, CLI inspection/clearing, and cached-token usage metrics. Caching defaults to disabled; when enabled, the defaults are 20 GiB and a 2,048-token interval.

Validation:
- 84 regular tests passed; 1 skipped.
- Both local 8B real-weight tests passed. Two 35B tests were explicitly skipped because the weights were unavailable.
- A 2,799-token coding fixture produced identical output tokens with caching disabled, on first write, on repeat, and after process restart.
- On an M5 MacBook Air with 24 GB RAM, measured TTFT was 6.51 s disabled, 6.77 s on first write, 0.50 s on repeat, and 0.61 s after restart. These are sequential single samples with a warm OS filesystem cache, not controlled cold-SSD measurements.

Publication increased peak MLX allocation by about 24% in this sample. Shared blocks are currently reserialized synchronously, so retained-storage deduplication does not eliminate write work. Real-weight 35B validation, short-prefix break-even measurements, and sustained/cold-filesystem trials remain outstanding. This does not add GGUF support, KV quantization, or active-context offloading.

Usage, raw benchmark results, and continuation limitations are documented in `docs/conversation-cache.md`, `docs/conversation-cache-results.md`, and `docs/benchmarks/conversation-cache-m5.json`.

pulls.title: backends/cuda: a torch reference backend — edge0-8b and edge0-35b generate text on an NVIDIA GPU
pulls.body:
## What

A torch backend for `edge0`, behind `EDGE0_BACKEND=cuda`, and the two model ports the
engines need. With it, **both engines — edge0-8b and edge0-35b — generate text on an NVIDIA
GPU**, checked against MLX at every level.

MLX's own CUDA backend does not get there at any version available today: the first
forward pass fails, differently at each version (`QMM NYI` at 0.30.4, no `GatherQMM` at
0.31.1, `SmallVector out of range` inside `core.eval` at 0.32.x). `docs/nvidia.md` keeps
that investigation so the next person doesn't repeat it.

Nothing changes for MLX users: `backends/mlx/` is untouched, the backend facade picks the
implementation, and `EDGE0_BACKEND` defaults to MLX.

**Scope.** This is a slow, eager, correctness-first *reference*, not the CUDA offload
redesign discussed in #18 and #20, and it keeps the existing streaming/mmap structure.
Its intended role is a second implementation to diff a faster CUDA path against, layer by
layer, on any machine with torch. Whether and how it fits is the question in #114; it can
be split if that is easier to review (see below).

## Layout

* `backends/cuda/{core,nn,io,quant}.py` — the backend contract on torch: MLX-named array
  ops, `RMSNorm`/`QuantizedLinear`/`QuantizedEmbedding` on the MLX quantization layout,
  `gather_qmm`, and a `load_model` that reads the published (MLX-format) checkpoints.
* `backends/cuda/_impl/bailing_hybrid.py`, `_impl/qwen3_5_moe.py` — torch ports of the
  vendored MLX backbones, same module tree, parameter names and call signatures, so
  `engine/ling.py` and `engine/qwen.py` run unchanged.
* `engine/`, `prerouter/`, `streaming/` — the small changes that let shared code run on
  either backend (no direct `mlx` imports, backend-dispatched model classes,
  class-level prerouter patch on the active backend). **These are the only edits to code
  MLX users run.**

## How it is checked

MLX **on the CPU** is the reference throughout: on some Apple GPUs MLX's float32
matmul/SDPA sits ~7e-4 from float64, while MLX-CPU and torch both sit ~2e-7, so a GPU
reference makes a correct port look worse than it is. The tests run each case under both
backends in subprocesses (`tests/test_backend_parity.py`, `tests/test_cuda_backend.py`):

| Piece | Against MLX |
|---|---|
| `gather_qmm` (2/4/8-bit affine, every broadcast shape the streaming layer uses), through both of its code paths | `mx.gather_qmm` |
| routing, sampling, `RMSNorm`, `gelu`, the prerouter's batched head at their real call sites | identical expert choices and sampler masks |
| `StreamingSwitchGLU`, all four paths, on layer 1 of the real edge0-8b checkpoint | 1.2–1.5% of output scale (about two bf16 ulps) |
| `bailing_hybrid` port, real edge0-8b weights, every layer, chunked prefill + decode | ≤ 1.5e-6 per layer, ≤ 1.7e-6 on the logits |
| `qwen3_5_moe` port, **real edge0-35b weights (19.5 GB)**, all 40 layers, 0 missing / 0 unexpected params | ≤ 2.4e-6 (GatedDeltaNet), ≤ 3.7e-6 (full attention), logits ≤ 2.4e-6, same argmax at every step |
| whole edge0-8b engine (LoRA, prerouter-staged decode, streaming) | identical greedy tokens (`pytest -m slow`) |
| whole edge0-35b engine (LoRA, 33 prerouter heads, streaming), 32 greedy tokens | 32/32 identical to MLX-CPU |
| **edge0-8b backbone on an NVIDIA GB10** (`sm_121`, torch 2.14+cu130), float32, each layer fed MLX's own input | **≤ 5.3e-7 per layer**, 4.3e-7 on the logits, same argmax |
| whole edge0-8b engine on that GPU, 32 greedy tokens | 31 of 32 identical to MLX |
| whole edge0-35b engine on that GPU, 32 greedy tokens | **32/32 identical**, 18.4 s |

The tests carry negative controls (the transformers norm convention, a wrong RoPE layout,
the prerouter disabled) so they are known to be discriminative rather than merely green.

Two notes on the token comparisons:

* edge0-8b step 31 is not a GPU artifact. Torch on a CPU sits at the same ~4.5% median
  per-step logit distance from MLX — the staged prerouter path drops experts it did not
  stage — and the top-2 margin at that step is below that noise.
* edge0-35b against MLX-**Metal** is 29/32, and Metal disagrees with MLX-**CPU** at exactly
  the same three positions, so that is MLX-GPU tie-breaking, not the port.

`EDGE0_TORCH_DEVICE` (`cpu` / `mps` / `cuda`) overrides device selection; running the
suite with `mps` is what catches host/device mistakes on a machine that has no CUDA.

## Speed

Still not a fast path, but no longer needlessly slow. Profiling edge0-8b decode on the
torch backend showed the CPU mostly *waiting*: of an 8.2 s run, 5.7 s were `nonzero` /
`tolist` / `unique` inside `gather_qmm`, each a device→host sync, one per expert, against
0.07 s for the matmuls they were arranging. Decode-sized calls now gather the rows'
experts as one batch and run a single `bmm` (the per-expert loop remains for prefill,
behind one host transfer; capped by rows and by bytes so a 35b expert cannot blow memory).
edge0-8b decode on Metal (`EDGE0_TORCH_DEVICE=mps`), same greedy tokens throughout:

| | ms/token |
|---|---|
| tier default (`cache_slots=64`) | 688 |
| + batched decode gather | 401 |
| + `cache_slots=3072` | 384 |
| + `EDGE0_TORCH_WEIGHT_CACHE=1` | 291 |

The GB10 timings in `docs/nvidia.md` predate this change and have not been re-measured.

## Status and limits

* Correctness is established for both engines on real weights; performance is not.
  `gather_qmm` and the quantized linears still dequantize on every call, and
  `core.compile` is eager. No fused dequantize+matmul, no graph capture.
* Batched independent contexts and long-context behaviour are untested.
* The two `gather_qmm` paths agree to float32 summation-order noise (~1e-5), not
  bit-for-bit.

Verified with `EDGE0_8B_MODEL` and `EDGE0_35B_MODEL` set: **122 passed, 2 skipped** on this
branch merged with current `main`, on the torch CPU device. The real-weights 35b test
needs ~22 GB of RAM for both models; without `EDGE0_35B_MODEL` it skips.

## Reviewing this in pieces

If the whole thing is too large to read at once, the natural seams are:

1. the backend facade + `backends/cuda/{core,nn,io,quant}` and their tests;
2. the two model ports;
3. the shared-code changes in `engine/`, `prerouter/`, `streaming/` (start here — the only
   part MLX users can feel);
4. docs.

I can split it along those lines on request.


### October 10 documentation follow-up

Updated the root and Python READMEs to describe the existing optional Torch CUDA reference backend rather than a reserved slot. This follow-up changes documentation only; the numerical results above are historical and were not rerun for this revision.

pulls.title: fix(streaming): give the hot stack its zero overflow row
pulls.body:
The hot-stack prefill path in `StreamingSwitchGLU.__call__` maps every routed expert that is not in the hot stack to row `n_rows = len(self._hot_key)` (the "overflow zero row"), runs the fast gather, and then adds the exact contribution of those misses on top. But `load_hot_layer` only builds `n_hot` rows, so every miss makes `gather_qmm` read past the end of the stack. MLX does not bounds-check gathers: the miss slots get whatever sits after the buffer, and the exact correction is added to that instead of to zero.

**Why it went unnoticed:** `test_hot_stack_matches_exact` loads every expert (`n_hot=N_EXPERTS`, "full coverage -> no misses"), so it never produces a miss. On a real checkpoint the result can come out right when the memory after the stack happens to be zero-filled.

**Repro** (current `main`, mlx 0.30.6, Apple M5 Max): same layer as the existing test, but with 4 of the 8 experts hot. At the miss slots the hot path returns values like `-3.6e35`, `8.5e37` and `nan`, where the exact path gives `~797`.

**Fix:** the numpy backing built by `load_hot_layer` carries one extra all-zero row, so the overflow row actually exists and contributes zero. This is the same idea as the staged path's `_zero_slot`. `_build` (slicing an expert out of the backing) and `materialize_hot` account for the extra row. The cost is one expert row per hot layer.

**Tests** (both run for the separate and fused gate/up layouts, and both fail before this change):
- `test_hot_stack_has_zero_overflow_row`: deterministic; the materialized stack has `n_hot + 1` rows and the last one is all zeros.
- `test_hot_stack_with_misses_matches_exact`: hot path == exact path when half the routed experts are misses.

Full suite passes, and so does `pytest -m slow` for edge0-8b.

**Heads-up:** #7 also edits the `_build` hot fast path, including the `per = buf.size // len(self._hot_key)` line this PR changes. Whichever merges second needs a trivial rebase.

pulls.title: Fix/35b nan hidden clip
pulls.body:
Fixes #11. Two independent defects — the prompt path that triggered the degenerate turns, and the NaN cascade that made them unrecoverable. Both are needed.

## 1. `ChatSession.prompt_ids` threw away the rendered template (`server/chat.py`)

`try/except/else` was inverted: an `else` clause on `try` runs when **no** exception was raised, so the successful render was discarded and replaced by the hardcoded ChatML from `_chat_text()`.

The qwen35 template ends the generation prompt with an empty think block (`<think>\n\n</think>\n\n` for `enable_thinking=False`); the hardcoded string stops at `<|im_start|>assistant`. The model therefore opened its own `<think>` (leaking into `content`) and some turns derailed into empty or two-token replies — the `!` collapse was the extreme case of that. The render is now kept, and `_chat_text()` is only the fallback for a tokenizer with no template (or a failing render); that also removes the unbound `text` `NameError` on that path.

Regression guard in `tests/test_server.py`: `FakeTok` records the text it is asked to encode, so the assertions check *what is actually encoded* (template vs ChatML), and `PlainTok` is a standalone class — the old `del self.apply_chat_template` raised `AttributeError` on an inherited method and was swallowed, so the fallback path had never been exercised. Both new assertions fail against the old code (`AssertionError` and `UnboundLocalError`).

## 2. All-NaN logits collapsed the answer into `!` (`_impl/qwen3_5.py`, `engine/qwen.py`)

Instrumenting `_forward` on 35b shows the mechanism: a prefill overflow inside one layer (layer 10, a linear-attention layer) leaves 8 of its 15 rows NaN; every later layer then produces all-NaN from that NaN input; the `lm_head` logits are fully NaN (248320 = the whole vocab) and `argmax` falls back to token 0, which decodes to `!` for the rest of the request — and never recovers, because the poisoned state is reused by later requests.

This is the pathology the ling tier already guards with `LING_HIDDEN_CLIP`; the 35b path had no equivalent. It now clamps each layer's output to [-v, +v] and scrubs NaN entries, gated by `QWEN_HIDDEN_CLIP` and defaulted to 1000 by the engine (deployers can override it, or set 0 to disable).

## Verification (Mac mini M4 Pro, `applegpu_g16s`, mlx 0.30.6)

| check | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| the issue's 4-question serve sequence over HTTP | `<think>` leak, then `!` from req3 on | 4/4 fluent, no `<think>` leak |
| 4 questions x 3 rounds through `ChatSession` | collapses | 0 bad of 12 |
| same prompt x6 | collapses | 6/6 ok |
| greedy (temperature 0), the 4 questions | — | all four correct |
| `pytest` | 60 passed / 1 skipped | 60 passed / 1 skipped |

pulls.title: perf: prepare typed mmap expert reads once per layer
pulls.body:
## Change

Prepare typed, immutable mmap row readers once per streaming layer. `_build` then reads the selected expert directly, with the shard, offset, stride, count, and dtype already resolved. This removes repeated tensor-name lookup, metadata arithmetic, and intermediate byte views from the warm-file cache-miss path.

The source payload, quantization, routing, output shapes, MLX conversion, and matrix kernels are unchanged. Fused gate/up retains the original row order. The hot-stack path is unchanged. Each layer adds nine small metadata descriptors; preparing them reads no weight payload and retains no exported mmap view.

## Correctness

For tensor offset O, row stride B, and expert i, both implementations read exactly `[O+i*B, O+(i+1)*B)`, with the same dtype and reshape. NumPy integer indices are normalized before offset arithmetic so narrow integer widths cannot wrap.

Local validation: **97 passed, 1 existing skip, 2 slow tests deselected**. The unchanged baseline passes 60 tests in the same environment. Added coverage includes payload bit equality, all NumPy integer widths, concurrent readers, buffer lifetime/close behavior, bounds, separate/fused paths, and multi-shard forward equality.

The benchmark also compares every tensor bit for nine published Edge0 expert payloads before timing. The frozen baseline is the complete `_build` from `fbab5f8c08e843e204c0fc6ae18b89a154c652cf`; its executable AST was verified against that revision. Both measured functions are equally bound methods on the same layer and mmap.

## Measured improvement

Four final runs contain **328 paired timing blocks and 65,600 timed expert builds**, including MLX array creation and `eval`.

| Public-weight case | Median paired time reduction |
|---|---:|
| Serial separate, two independent runs | 7.18% and 11.74% |
| Serial fused gate/up, two independent runs | 7.13% and 5.75% |
| Four-worker batch, separate | 5.32% |
| Four-worker batch, fused gate/up | 5.25% |

All recorded 95% paired bootstrap intervals have positive lower bounds. A seeded synthetic-weight control also improves. Full settings, source-weight revision, every paired observation, and reproduction commands are in `docs/benchmarks/expert-read-plan.md`, with a standalone benchmark in `scripts/bench_expert_reads.py`.

These are host-side materialization measurements on a live Linux i5-3470 workstation using MLX CPU 0.30.4. Compilation was disabled equally for both paths due to a pinned Linux CPU JIT/compiler compatibility issue. This patch does not alter compile settings. End-to-end tokens/s, cold-SSD performance, GPU/iPhone speed, and increased model capacity are unmeasured.

```sh
PYTHONPATH=src python scripts/bench_expert_reads.py --out serial.json
PYTHONPATH=src python scripts/bench_expert_reads.py --workers 4 --batch-size 4 --out threaded.json
pytest -m 'not slow'
```

The default benchmark creates its own deterministic fixture and requires no checkpoint download.

pulls.title: perf(streaming): page-granular mmap warming with exactness tests and benchmarks
pulls.body:
## Summary

Reduce host-side mmap warming work without changing model weights, routing, cache policy, quantization, or inference arithmetic.

- Add `SafetensorsMmap.touch(offset, length)`: read exactly one byte per intersecting OS page, using `mmap.PAGESIZE`, with unaligned-tail and empty-range handling.
- Replace `seq_read()` chunk-sized byte copies with page reads while preserving its traversal-window argument.
- Replace the ignored full-byte sums in `StreamingSwitchGLU.warm_pages()` with exact expert-range page reads.
- Add backend-free page-coverage tests, MLX integration checks, paired benchmarks, and raw results. Linux CI runs the new backend-free tests.

The relevant entry points are explicit expert warming and Ling's `EDGE0_PREWARM=1` startup path. This is a warming/preparation optimization, not a claimed decoder-token-rate or model-capacity gain.

## Measured improvement

Intel i5-3470 Linux host, 4 KiB pages, Python 3.12.13, NumPy 2.5.3. Comparisons randomize baseline/candidate order within each pair against the implementations at `fbab5f8c08e843e204c0fc6ae18b89a154c652cf`.

| Path | Baseline median | Candidate median |
|---|---:|---:|
| Resident 128 MiB shard warming | 29.731 ms | 0.481 ms |
| Resident 512 MiB shard warming | 75.361 ms | 1.971 ms |
| Explicit warming + four real expert builds + MLX CPU evaluation | 5.593 ms | 1.767 ms |
| Default warming's peak traced allocation | 33,554,602 bytes | 34,352 bytes |

The real-weight preparation test has 31 randomized pairs and a median paired time reduction of **68.38%**, bootstrap 95% interval **68.20%–68.53%**. A separate-process reproduction measured 73.89%; both raw runs are included.

Cold-file-page-cache controls show **no clear speed advantage**: the 128 MiB paired interval is [-2.65%, +0.37%], and the 512 MiB interval is [-7.05%, +11.44%]. All cold samples begin at zero resident pages, checked with Linux `mincore`. Only the benchmark's own temporary file is evicted. The result does not imply less physical disk traffic.

## Correctness

- Instrumented execution verifies exact page coverage for 4 KiB and 16 KiB pages, with 1,000 random ranges per page size plus boundary cases.
- Both whole-shard paths leave all 32,769 / 131,073 fixture pages resident, with unchanged input SHA-256.
- 81 materialized tensors from nine published Edge0 experts match byte-for-byte before/after warming.
- 12 real-expert SwiGLU comparisons with synthetic inputs match exactly.
- Backend-free mmap/hygiene tests: **27 passed**.
- Full suite with pinned MLX 0.30.4 / MLX-LM 0.31.0 on CPU eager execution: **87 passed, 1 skipped, 2 slow tests deselected**. Matched upstream: 60 passed, 1 skipped, 2 deselected.

On this host, GCC 15 rejects duplicate floating-point typedefs in MLX 0.30.4's bundled CPU JIT preamble. The same 14 streaming-math failures occur on unchanged upstream. Successful CPU tests disable compilation in the test harness only. Production compilation and dependency pins are unchanged; the existing macOS CI remains the compiled/Metal validation path.

## Reproduction

See `docs/benchmarks/page-warmup.md`, `scripts/bench_page_warmup.py`, and the optional small real-weight probe. The real-weight downloader fetches about 16 MB of pinned public ranges, not the complete checkpoint. Raw timing samples and controls are in `docs/benchmarks/page-warmup/`.
